title: How to use AI safely with your personal information
problems: The claim "In Claude, look for a 'Temporary Chat' button next to 'New Chat' in the sidebar" is fabricated. Claude (claude.ai) does not currently offer a 'Temporary Chat' or 'Incognito Mode' feature in its user interface, nor is there a button labeled 'Temporary Chat' next to 'New Chat' in the sidebar.

title: Ask Copilot to compare two product specs and list the differences
problems: The article describes GitHub Copilot as having a general-purpose web chat interface accessible via URLs like 'copilot.github.com' or 'github.com/copilot' that can browse arbitrary web pages, extract information, and compare them. GitHub Copilot is primarily an AI pair programmer integrated into IDEs and does not possess this described web browsing or standalone general-purpose chat capability for arbitrary URLs.

The URLs 'copilot.github.com' and 'github.com/copilot' are mentioned as entry points for a web-based chat interface where users can paste links for comparison. These URLs do not lead to such a functional web chat for GitHub Copilot.

The described UI elements such as 'a chat box that says “Ask Copilot anything…” in the middle of the page' at 'copilot.github.com' or 'open the Copilot chat from the GitHub homepage' for browsing external web pages do not exist for GitHub Copilot.

title: Turn your Zoom call into meeting minutes in 5 minutes with Grok
problems: Claim: "Grok is free to use." This is false. Grok is only available to X Premium+ subscribers, which is a paid tier.

Claim: "Go to grok.com in your browser and sign in with your xAI account." This is an incorrect URL for accessing Grok. Grok is accessed via the X (formerly Twitter) platform for Premium+ subscribers, not a dedicated `grok.com` chat portal. `grok.com` redirects to `x.ai` (xAI's corporate site).

Claim: "Tap New chat or click the plus icon to begin a fresh conversation" for Grok. The description of Grok's user interface (implying a standalone chat application with a 'New chat' button) does not accurately reflect how Grok is integrated into the X platform for Premium+ users.

Claim: Grok can accept uploaded MP4 files (audio/video) for transcription and summarization. This is a fabricated feature. Grok does not currently support direct audio or video file uploads for processing into meeting minutes.

title: Turn a short note into a polished email reply with Meta AI in Outlook
problems: The article describes a specific UI element: a "light grey box labelled Meta AI draft" that appears directly below your typed message within Microsoft Outlook's email reply box. This box is described as actively "watching" your text and generating/updating email drafts based on in-line prompts (e.g., "Meta AI, turn this into a friendly email reply"). Meta AI does not have this direct, interactive integration feature within Microsoft Outlook. While Microsoft's own AI (Copilot) provides similar functionality within Outlook, Meta AI is a separate product and does not offer this specific UI or workflow integration.

The instructions imply that by typing "Meta AI, [instruction]" directly into the Outlook reply box, Meta AI will process the command and update the draft in the grey box. This is a fabricated interaction for Meta AI within Outlook.

title: Brainstorm startup names with one Grok prompt on X
problems: The claim "An X account (free) with Grok enabled" is inaccurate. Grok access requires an X Premium+ subscription, which is a paid service, not simply a free account with Grok 'enabled'.

The article suggests Grok can "Suggest 5 more names similar to [name] that are available as .com domains." Grok, as an LLM, cannot perform real-time domain availability checks; it can only suggest names based on its training data, not confirm their current availability. This feature is not possessed by Grok.

title: Build a smart recipe finder that suggests meals from ingredients in the Home app
problems: The Home app does not have the functionality to add a 'pantry' or 'fridge' as an item that then allows users to list individual food ingredients within it. Its purpose is for managing smart home accessories, not inventory.
The described UI elements, such as a 'detail view' for a pantry/fridge item showing a list of ingredients (e.g., 'Eggs', 'Cheddar cheese'), do not exist in the Apple Home app.

The 'sparkle icon' or 'Ask Apple Intelligence' button within a Home app pantry/fridge view that leads to a text box for ingredient-based recipe prompts is a fabricated UI element and interaction flow. Apple Intelligence does not integrate with the Home app in this specific manner.

The 'recipe card' UI, 'bookmark icon' or 'Save' button for saving AI-generated recipes within the Home app, and the 'Saved to Recipes' confirmation banner are fabricated UI elements and functionality.
The automatic saving of an AI-generated recipe from the Home app to Apple Notes, as described, is a fabricated integration and feature. The Home app does not have this capability.

title: How to analyse files and spreadsheets with ChatGPT
problems: Claim that file analysis and chart generation features work on the free tier of ChatGPT: These capabilities (Advanced Data Analysis) are exclusive to paid ChatGPT subscriptions (Plus, Team, Enterprise) and are not available on the free tier (ChatGPT 3.5).

Claim that 'Simple charts are supported on both free and paid tiers': Chart generation from uploaded files is part of the Advanced Data Analysis feature, which is only available on paid tiers of ChatGPT.

title: Organise your work with Claude Projects – a step‑by‑step beginner’s guide
problems: The existence of 'Claude Projects' as a feature in Anthropic Claude: Claude does not have a native feature called 'Projects' that allows users to create a dedicated workspace to group multiple chat sessions and files for combined querying and management.

UI elements and workflow described for 'Claude Projects': The article details specific UI elements such as a 'grid of four squares' icon leading to a 'Projects' sidebar, '+ New Project' buttons, 'Add conversation' buttons with checkboxes for linking multiple existing chats, and a 'Share Project' button with link/email invite options. These UI elements and the described workflow for managing and querying across multiple chats and files within a 'Project' workspace do not exist in Claude.

title: Create a tiny AI weather-helper widget for your blog with Hugging Face widgets
problems: The UI elements and workflow described for accessing a 'Widgets gallery' on Hugging Face are fabricated. There is no 'Widgets' link in the left sidebar under 'Resources', nor a dedicated 'Widgets gallery' page on Hugging Face for pre-made, no-code utility widgets like a weather helper. Hugging Face offers embedding options for specific models or 'Spaces' (interactive ML apps), but not a general gallery of such widgets.

The 'Weather widget' itself, with its specific detail page, settings (Location, Units, Theme), and live preview, is an invented feature attributed to Hugging Face within the fabricated 'Widgets gallery' context.

title: Create catchy Instagram captions using AI in minutes – a beginner’s guide
problems: The article describes a Meta AI navigation menu containing options like "Chat", "Image", and "Caption". Meta AI primarily functions as a conversational AI; its web interface (ai.meta.com) does not feature distinct navigation options or tools specifically labeled "Image" and "Caption" in this manner.

The article claims there is a dedicated "Caption Generator" tool on the Meta AI homepage, appearing as a tile or an icon resembling a speech bubble with a pencil. Meta AI does not have such a dedicated, distinct tool or UI element for caption generation; captions are generated through conversational prompts.

The article details a specific user interface for the supposed "Caption Generator" tool, including a text box prompting "Describe your image" and a dedicated "Generate" button. This UI description is fabricated as no such specific tool exists within Meta AI's interface.

The article states as fact that "Some free accounts limit the number of generations per day – if you hit that limit, the message will tell you to try again tomorrow" and advises users to "shorten your prompt to use fewer generations" if a "limit reached" notice appears. Meta AI does not publicly advertise or commonly enforce such daily generation limits for basic text prompts like caption creation, nor does it typically display a 'limit reached' notice for this type of usage.

title: Getting started with DeepSeek for everyday help
problems: The claim that there is an official DeepSeek app available for download on smartphones or tablets from app stores is fabricated. DeepSeek is primarily a web-based platform.

The description of a 'Deep Think' toggle switch or button (or variations like 'Reasoning Mode', 'Plan & Execute') in the DeepSeek chat interface is fabricated. DeepSeek's models have reasoning capabilities, but there is no explicit user-facing UI element called 'Deep Think' that users can toggle.

The description of a collapsible 'Thought Process' or 'Steps Taken' section that explicitly displays DeepSeek's internal reasoning steps before the final answer is fabricated. While some AI models might show intermediate steps, this specific UI element and feature as described does not exist in the DeepSeek chat interface.

title: Polish your writing instantly with GitHub Copilot
problems: Invented URL / domains: The URL `copilot.github.com` is presented as a direct, interactive chat interface for GitHub Copilot for general text editing. This is incorrect; `copilot.github.com` redirects to a marketing page, not a chat panel.

Invented UI elements/buttons/menus/pages: The article describes a specific user interface for a 'Copilot chat on the GitHub website' at `copilot.github.com`, including a 'white chat panel and a blinking cursor', a 'text entry field at the bottom of the chat', and specific 'Copy' icons or 'Regenerate/Edit again' buttons for general text editing. This chat interface does not exist as described at that URL for this purpose.

Invented prices, discounts, percentages or plan claims stated as fact: The claim that 'the first few prompts are free; larger usage may need a paid plan' for the described 'Copilot chat on the GitHub website' is false. GitHub Copilot requires a paid subscription for its core functionalities, including chat in IDEs or features within GitHub.com; there is no general freemium chat experience as described for arbitrary text editing.

title: Generate AI-powered tweet threads on X with Grok
problems: The claim "A free xAI account (sign up with email or X)" is incorrect. Grok is not available via a free, standalone xAI account; it requires an X Premium+ subscription.
The statement "Grok is free to use, but some advanced features may require a paid plan" is incorrect. Grok is exclusively available to X Premium+ subscribers and is not offered as a free service.

title: Getting Started with Grok: Your Guide to Everyday AI Answers
problems: The article invents the names of Grok's conversation modes. It states that users will find "Regular Mode" and "Fun Mode" for Grok's personality settings. In reality, Grok's conversation modes are named "Do Not Grok" (for direct, factual answers) and "Grok" (for more creative, often sarcastic responses).

title: Build a simple weekly study plan with Meta AI in 10 minutes
problems: The claim that "Meta AI will reply with a colour-coded weekly calendar" is fabricated. Meta AI, like other chatbots, generates text. It can describe a colour-coded calendar in text, but it does not render a visual, colour-coded calendar directly within the chat interface.

The claim that a "share icon" will provide an option to "Save as image" for the text-based study plan is fabricated. While users can screenshot the chat, Meta AI does not offer a built-in feature to save its text output as an image.

The claim that users can "ask Meta AI to 'turn the plan into voice reminders' and follow the link it provides" is fabricated. Meta AI does not currently have the capability to generate a link that directly sets up voice reminders on a user's phone based on a generated plan.

title: How to run your first open‑source LLM from DeepSeek on a home PC
problems: The article repeatedly references specific DeepSeek model names like `deepseek-r1:1.5b` and `deepseek-r1:8b` that are intended to be run via the Ollama tool (e.g., in the command `ollama run deepseek-r1:1.5b`). However, the model name `deepseek-r1` with these specific tags is not found in Ollama's official model library for DeepSeek. While DeepSeek has various open-source models and Ollama can run them, the particular model identifier provided in the guide is invented.

title: Turn a blurry photo into a crisp poster with NVIDIA AI Image Super‑Resolution in 5 minutes
problems: The core claim that ChatRTX offers 'NVIDIA AI Image Super-Resolution' to sharpen photos is fabricated. ChatRTX is a local RAG chatbot designed for processing text-based data with LLMs, not an image editing or image super-resolution tool.

The article claims a 'free NVIDIA account' and a 'Sign In' or 'Log In' button/screen are required in ChatRTX. This is fabricated. ChatRTX runs locally and does not require an NVIDIA account or any sign-in process to function.

The article describes a `/upload myphoto.jpg` command, a file-picker, and a 'paperclip icon or a button like Attach' within ChatRTX for image files. These UI elements and commands are fabricated. ChatRTX's interface is for text input and connecting to text-based data sources (local folders, YouTube URLs), not for uploading or processing image files for super-resolution.

The claim that typing `Make this photo sharp and poster-ready at 4K resolution` into ChatRTX will cause it to process and upscale an image is fabricated. As a text-based chatbot, ChatRTX cannot interpret or act on such a command to perform image upscaling, nor does it possess image processing capabilities.

The descriptions of a 'progress bar' appearing under an image and a 'new, sharper version of your photo appear below the original' within ChatRTX are fabricated, as the tool does not perform image upscaling.

title: Turn a messy email into a clear bullet-point list with Hugging Face’s free summarizer
problems: The article states that 'A free Hugging Face account' is a prerequisite to use the summarizer demo at https://huggingface.co/spaces/facebook/bart-large-cnn. This specific Hugging Face Space can be used by anyone anonymously without requiring a Hugging Face account, making this claim fabricated.

title: How to use Le Chat to translate a whole webpage in one click
problems: The UI description of Le Chat's entry point and chat window is inaccurate: While mistral.ai has a 'Try Le Chat' button, it redirects to chat.mistral.ai as a full page, not an overlay chat window on the right side of the mistral.ai homepage.
Le Chat does not have the feature to display 'a preview of the webpage appear in the chat' when a URL is pasted. It cannot fetch and visually render an entire webpage within its chat interface.

Le Chat does not possess the feature to 'Translate this entire page' while preserving 'clear headings and paragraphs' and 'even some formatting' within the chat interface. While LLMs can process text from URLs (if browsed), they do not function as full webpage translation and rendering tools that output a formatted, translated version of the entire page directly into the chat.

title: How to Use Project Genie with Street View
problems: The article describes 'Project Genie' as a publicly accessible, web-based tool within Google Labs or AI Test Kitchen with specific UI elements (upload image buttons, physics brush tools, generate/play buttons, a dashboard) and a user workflow. While Google DeepMind has published research on a 'Genie' model capable of generating playable 2D worlds from images, there is no evidence of a publicly available 'Project Genie' product or experiment with the described user interface, access points (e.g., via labs.google), or functionality for the general public to use as detailed.

The URL/access method described for 'Project Genie' (searching for 'Google Project Genie' or 'Google AI Test Kitchen' to find an official Google Labs page for Project Genie with a link directly from `labs.google`) is invented. There is no such public `labs.google` page or direct public access interface for 'Project Genie' as described.

title: Add a friendly FAQ chatbot to your site with DeepSeek in 10 minutes
problems: UI elements/buttons/menus/pages described for a named product that do not exist: The entire described workflow of a "bot dashboard" with "Create Bot" or "New Bot" buttons, fields for "Bot Name," "Description," and "Knowledge Base," and tabs for "Settings," "Knowledge," and "Deploy" are fabricated. DeepSeek is an LLM provider and does not offer a no-code chatbot builder platform with these specific UI elements for end-users to manage and deploy chat widgets.

UI elements/buttons/menus/pages described for a named product that do not exist: The "Knowledge" section with a box to paste text, "Save" or "Update Knowledge" buttons, and settings like "Answer Style," "Response Tone," "Context Window," and a "Train" or "Update Model" button do not exist on DeepSeek's platform.

UI elements/buttons/menus/pages described for a named product that do not exist: The "Deploy" tab with a chat widget preview, options for "Widget Colour," "Greeting Message," "Position on Page," and a "Generate Code" button does not exist on DeepSeek's platform.

invented or wrong URLs / domains: The example HTML `<script src="https://api.deepseek.com/widget.js" async></script>` uses an invented URL for a DeepSeek chat widget script. DeepSeek provides API endpoints for model inference, not a pre-built `widget.js` for direct embedding.

title: Set up a local AI assistant with NVIDIA ChatRTX on your PC
problems: The article claims NVIDIA ChatRTX will "typically prompt you to sign in to your NVIDIA account" upon launch, requiring email and password entry with "Sign In" or "Log In" buttons. NVIDIA ChatRTX is a local application and does not require an in-app sign-in to an NVIDIA account for its core functionality.

The article attributes a smart device control feature to ChatRTX, describing a "Tools" menu, "Device Manager" option, and "Add Device" or "Connect New Device" buttons for linking and controlling smart home devices. ChatRTX does not have native smart home integration features or the described UI elements; its primary function is local large language model (LLM) inference and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).

title: Build a simple AI habit tracker with Siri on your iPhone
problems: The article attributes the feature of "learning your routine and nudging you at the right moment" to the specific habit tracker built using Apple Intelligence and Siri Shortcuts in the hook. However, the provided steps for building the shortcut do not implement any such dynamic learning or intelligent nudging using Apple Intelligence; the reminder is either manually triggered or set to a fixed schedule via an alarm.

Step 6, titled "Add the Apple Intelligence check," implies a specific Apple Intelligence action or integration. However, the described actions (adding an 'If' block) use standard Siri Shortcuts logic and do not involve any explicit Apple Intelligence component or 'check' as part of the shortcut.

The description of the 'If' condition UI in Step 6 is inaccurate. When setting a condition in the Shortcuts 'If' action, the path 'Scripting → Text → Contains' does not exist. Users directly select the value for comparison and then the comparison operator.

title: Turn long PDFs or Word files into a quick summary with Mistral AI
problems: The article claims users can 'Attach your PDF or Word file to the chat' on chat.mistral.ai using an 'attachment button' (paper-clip, plus sign, or upward-arrow icon) next to the message box. Mistral AI's public chat interface (chat.mistral.ai) does not support direct file uploads (PDF or DOCX) nor does it have an attachment button for this purpose. This is an invented UI element and a feature attributed to the tool that it does not possess.

The article describes a 'tiny thumbnail with the filename' appearing above the message box after attaching a file on chat.mistral.ai. This UI element does not exist because the file upload feature itself is not present on the platform.

title: How to plan meals and a grocery budget with AI
problems: The claim that general AI chat tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) can reliably "tell me the total cost in Australian dollars using typical supermarket prices" (stated in Step 4 and reinforced in the Common Mistakes section). These tools do not have real-time access to supermarket pricing data and cannot provide accurate or verifiable budgets based on current typical local prices. They can only generate plausible-looking but invented prices based on their training data, which often results in fabrication rather than actual 'typical supermarket prices'.

title: Activate Apple Intelligence on Your iPhone: A Beginner’s Step‑by‑Step Guide
problems: The claim that there is a 'new section titled Apple Intelligence with a switch labelled Enable Apple Intelligence' within Siri & Search settings is fabricated. Apple Intelligence is deeply integrated into iOS 18, but there is no single master 'Enable Apple Intelligence' toggle in Siri & Search.

The description of a three-dot menu (⋮) and 'Advanced Settings' for the Apple Intelligence section in Siri & Search is fabricated; this UI element and nesting do not exist for managing Apple Intelligence.

The claim that 'Intelligent Suggestions' in Siri & Search contains checkboxes for 'Message Drafts' and 'Mail Summaries' is incorrect. These specific Apple Intelligence writing tools are not controlled via individual checkboxes in this section; 'Intelligent Suggestions' primarily relates to Siri's app and shortcut suggestions.
The UI element of 'sliders instead of checkboxes' for controlling Apple Intelligence features under Intelligent Suggestions is fabricated.

The instruction to 'Press and hold [the mic icon] then say “Hey Siri, draft a friendly reply”' for message drafting is incorrect. The mic icon on the keyboard is for dictation, which converts speech directly to text. Apple Intelligence's writing tools are typically accessed via the magic wand icon or by explicitly invoking Siri, not by using the dictation mic for drafting prompts.

title: Quickly compare two holiday cities using Qwen Chat
problems: The article claims users can 'Continue as guest' on Qwen Chat. Qwen Chat (qwen.chat) requires users to log in with an Alibaba Cloud, Taobao, or Alipay account, or a phone number; it does not offer a 'Continue as guest' option for full chat functionality.
The article mentions a 'Summarise button above the reply' in Qwen Chat. The Qwen Chat user interface does not feature a dedicated 'Summarise' button above its responses.

The article states that 'a Table icon appears in the toolbar above the reply' in Qwen Chat for formatting output. The Qwen Chat user interface does not have a 'Table' icon in a toolbar above its replies.

title: Automate meeting note-taking with Microsoft Copilot in Teams
problems: The article describes a 'Share,' 'Export,' or 'Send to Outlook' button or link within the Teams meeting 'Recap' tab that automatically creates a new draft email in Outlook, pre-filled with the meeting summary, action items, and key decisions. This specific UI element and direct functionality to export the full structured Copilot notes from the Teams Recap tab into a pre-filled Outlook email draft does not exist as described. Users can copy parts of the recap or share a link to the recap within Teams, but there isn't a one-click button that performs this auto-drafting in Outlook.

title: Build a quick project timeline outline using Grok on X
problems: The claim "A free or paid xAI account (the free tier is enough for a short timeline)" is fabricated. Grok is currently a feature of X Premium, which requires a paid subscription; there is no free tier for Grok access.

The description of alternative UI elements for accessing Grok, specifically "If you don’t see a robot head, look for a button labelled “AI Assistant” or a similar icon with three dots that opens a menu where “Grok” is listed," is fabricated. Grok typically has a distinct, direct link in the left-hand navigation for subscribers, not a generic 'AI Assistant' button or a three-dot menu leading to it in this context.

The guide attributes 'Save' and 'Share' functionality, including a 'Share' button to add colleagues’ email addresses, to the Grok interface on X, stating: "Finally, give the document a clear name such as 'July‑August Launch Timeline' and hit Save. If you work with a team, click the “Share” button (usually a silhouette with a + sign) and add colleagues’ email addresses." Grok is a chat assistant and does not have built-in document saving or sharing features for its generated responses; these actions would be performed in the external planner or spreadsheet where the user pastes the content.

title: Build a Basic AI Chatbot Brain Using OpenAI's API – Quick Start
problems: The guide specifies 'tool: ChatGPT' but describes steps that are exclusive to the OpenAI API platform and Playground (e.g., getting API keys, navigating to the 'Playground', using 'System' and 'User' message boxes within the Playground's 'Chat' mode). These features and UI elements do not exist within the consumer-facing ChatGPT product (chat.openai.com).

title: Build simple community event flyers with Meta AI’s design prompts
problems: The article claims Meta AI can reliably generate flyers with multiple distinct, specific, and legible text elements (e.g., title, date, time, location, additional phrases like "Bring a blanket") clearly embedded within the image from a simple text prompt. Current Meta AI image generation models, while capable of generating images, are not consistently able to render multiple specific pieces of text accurately, legibly, and correctly placed as described for a flyer. Users frequently encounter garbled text, misspellings, or inability to place text precisely when attempting this with current generative AI models.

title: How to create and edit images in ChatGPT
problems: The description of a 'small icon that resembles a camera or a paintbrush' in the chat input box that users should click to 'Choose the image creation mode' is inaccurate. In ChatGPT, image generation is typically accessed by selecting a model (like GPT-4, which integrates DALL-E 3) from the model selector at the top of the interface, or by choosing a specific DALL-E custom GPT, rather than clicking a dedicated 'camera or paintbrush' icon within the main chat input box to switch modes.

title: Control your TV and streaming apps with Alexa voice commands
problems: In Step 2, the described UI flow for enabling voice control for streaming apps, specifically 'In the Alexa app, go to Devices → choose your TV → tap Enable voice control' which then presents a list of apps to toggle, is an invented UI element/flow. The Alexa app does not typically feature a universal 'Enable voice control' button under a specific TV device's settings that then shows a toggle list for individual streaming applications. Voice control for streaming apps is generally managed either natively by Fire TV devices, by linking specific streaming service accounts in the main Alexa app's 'TV & Video' settings, or through specific smart TV brand skills.

title: Getting started with Microsoft Copilot in everyday apps
problems: In Step 4 (PowerPoint), the article suggests looking for 'Designer' or 'Ideas' buttons as alternatives or links to Copilot. 'Designer' and 'Ideas' are distinct AI-powered features in PowerPoint, but they are not the Copilot interface or entry points to Copilot itself. Copilot has its own dedicated button.

title: Build a recipe generator that only uses what you already own with NVIDIA ChatRTX
problems: The UI buttons described as "Load Local File" and "Add Document" for adding files to ChatRTX do not exist. NVIDIA ChatRTX uses buttons like "Add Source" or "+ Add Source."

The claim that "only files with 'recipes' or 'pantry' in their names will work" for loading sources in ChatRTX is fabricated. ChatRTX can process any valid text file added as a source, regardless of its name.

The notification "Pantry loaded" is described as appearing "in the chat area" when a file is picked. ChatRTX typically shows generic notifications like "Source added" as a toast message, not directly in the chat area.

title: Build Your Own Text Summariser with Hugging Face (No Code)
problems: The article claims that users might encounter 'Spaces that require a paid plan' or that 'Some Spaces advertise premium features like higher-speed processing' which would require them to 'sign up for the free Hugging Face plan' or look for a 'free-tier Space'. Public Hugging Face Spaces are generally free to use for end-users, and there is no common UI element on Space cards that indicates a 'paid plan' for accessing or using a specific community demo. While Hugging Face offers paid 'Pro' plans, these provide benefits for the user's own account (e.g., faster inference for their own models, private Spaces), not a payment gateway for accessing public community-built demos.

title: Create your own weekly workout plan in 10 minutes with Le Chat
problems: The article states "Open your web browser or the Le Chat app on your phone". Mistral AI's Le Chat is currently a web-based interface and does not offer a dedicated, official mobile application. Users access Le Chat via a web browser on their phone, not a standalone app.

title: Create a multi‑room music playlist with Alexa+
problems: The UI flow described in Steps 2 and 3 for initiating a routine is incorrect. There is no 'Add to Routine' option when viewing a specific room's details or settings menu (accessed via a three-dot or gear icon) in the Alexa app. Routines are created by navigating to the 'More' tab at the bottom of the app, then selecting 'Routines', and then adding a new routine.

The UI described in Step 7 for selecting devices is inaccurate. In the Alexa app's routine 'Music' action, the selection of multiple devices/rooms for multi-room music is integrated directly into the same screen where you specify the music source (e.g., a playlist), typically under a 'From' section, not as a separate 'Choose devices' screen with checkboxes that appears after selecting a playlist.

title: Create a Smart-Home Security Alert with Alexa Routines
problems: The tool is referred to as "Alexa+". There is no official Amazon product or service branded "Alexa+". The article describes features of the standard Amazon Alexa app and ecosystem, which is simply referred to as "Alexa" or "Amazon Alexa".

title: Summarise Apple Calendar Events with Apple Intelligence
problems: The core feature: Apple Intelligence's ability to summarize Apple Calendar events directly within the Apple Calendar app, as described, has not been announced or demonstrated by Apple as a current or upcoming feature. While Apple Intelligence offers summarization in other apps (like Notes, Mail, Safari, Messages), a dedicated 'Summarise' button or automatic summarization for Calendar events is not a publicly known feature.

The UI elements described within the Apple Calendar app for summarization (e.g., a 'Summarise' or 'Generate Notes' button, 'Meeting Summary' section, 'Regenerate' or 'Improve' buttons) do not exist for this functionality, as the underlying feature itself is not announced.

The described UI paths and settings for enabling automatic event summaries (e.g., 'Settings > Calendar > Summaries > Summarise Events' on iOS/iPadOS or 'Calendar app > Settings > Advanced > Summarise Events' on macOS) are fabricated. These settings do not exist for Apple Calendar as part of Apple Intelligence features.

title: Create Royalty-Free AI Music Loops for Podcasts and Videos
problems: The article suggests that Suno.ai might have a dedicated 'loop' checkbox or setting ('If the tool has a dedicated "loop" checkbox or setting, ensure it's ticked before generating.') However, Suno.ai does not currently offer a specific UI element or checkbox for generating seamless loops; users rely on prompt engineering for this functionality.

title: Draft meeting agendas with Mistral’s Le Chat for office teams
problems: The claim that users need a 'free Mistral account' and can sign up at 'mistral.ai' to access a 'free tier' for Le Chat is fabricated. Mistral AI's (mistral.ai) primary focus is on models via API for developers and enterprises, and it does not offer a persistent, free conversational AI product like Le Chat accessible through a general user account with a 'free tier' on its main website. Le Chat was a temporary public demo available on a separate domain (lechat.mistral.ai), not as a standard product offering integrated with accounts on mistral.ai.

The described user interface flow for accessing Le Chat on 'mistral.ai' is fabricated. The article claims that after logging into 'mistral.ai', users would land on a 'dashboard page showing different Mistral products' and find a 'section or button labelled "Le Chat" or "Launch Le Chat"'. Such a dashboard and direct launch option for a conversational AI like Le Chat do not exist on the mistral.ai website for general public users.

title: Drafting Professional Presentations from Scratch Using Microsoft Copilot in PowerPoint
problems: The claim that "If you don’t have it [a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license], you’ll still be able to use basic Copilot features like generating outlines and slide titles" is incorrect. Copilot features in PowerPoint require a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license; there is no 'basic' tier of Copilot functionality available without this specific license within the Microsoft 365 applications.

title: How to Use Gemini Deep Research for Thorough Reports
problems: The article describes a UI element in Step 4 where Gemini shows 'a visual progress bar or a series of messages indicating what the AI is doing in real-time. These messages might pop up within the chat window, showing stages like "Searching for battery lifespans" or "Analysing recycling policies."'. Gemini typically indicates it's using Google Search or is in a 'Searching...' state, but it does not display granular, step-by-step progress messages for specific sub-tasks ('Searching for battery lifespans', 'Analysing recycling policies') within the chat window during the active search phase.

title: Using Gemini in Gmail and Docs to save time
problems: The claim that a Google Workspace user "can enable it in your account settings if it isn’t already" for Gemini is incorrect. For Google Workspace accounts (target audience 'business'), Gemini features are enabled by an administrator at the domain level, and users cannot typically enable it themselves from their personal account settings.

The description of the Google Docs UI in Step 3 for generating an outline is inaccurate: 'click the Gemini writing‑assistant icon that floats on the left‑hand margin' and 'clicking it opens a prompt pane on the right side of the document'. Gemini's 'Help me write' functionality for generating new content (like an outline) usually appears as an inline prompt directly within the document or via a toolbar button, rather than a floating left-margin icon opening a right-side pane. Additionally, stating it might be found under the 'Extensions' menu is misleading, as integrated Gemini features are not typically accessed as traditional extensions.

title: Generate spreadsheet formulas for common calculations using DeepSeek
problems: The article mentions a 'DeepSeek mobile app'. As of current information, DeepSeek primarily operates through a web interface and APIs, and there is no official, standalone 'DeepSeek mobile app' for its general LLM service.

title: Get quick answers to personal-finance questions with Mistral Le Chat
problems: The article mentions opening the "Le Chat app if you have it installed on your device". Mistral Le Chat does not offer a standalone mobile application; it is exclusively a web-based interface (which is mobile-responsive).

The article claims users can look for a "Share" icon, often an arrow pointing upwards out of a box, next to Mistral's reply. The Mistral Le Chat interface provides a 'Copy' button for individual responses, but not a distinct 'Share' button or icon as described.

title: Generate creative story ideas using DeepSeek’s chat interface
problems: The article claims that users can 'usually drag its top edge upwards' to resize the text input box in DeepSeek Chat. This UI element/behavior does not exist; the text input box in chat.deepseek.com automatically expands but is not manually resizable by dragging.

title: Get Started with xAI's Grok to Draft Professional Emails in Seconds
problems: The article claims Grok has explicit 'Standard' and 'Fun' writing modes or personality toggles in its user interface (Step 1). As of current knowledge, Grok does not feature these specific UI-selectable modes.

The article states Grok allows users to upload documents (like PDF, TXT, DOCX) for context via an attachment icon (Step 3). Grok, as integrated into X (formerly Twitter), does not currently support direct file uploads for contextual information.

title: Getting started with NVIDIA ChatRTX: a beginner's guide
problems: The article describes the ChatRTX download file as `chatrtx_server_xxx.zip`. The official download package typically starts with `NVIDIA_ChatRTX_` (e.g., `NVIDIA_ChatRTX_0.2.164.zip`). This is an invented filename.

The installation process described (extracting to `C:\ChatRTX` and running an `install.bat` file) is fabricated. ChatRTX uses a standard Windows executable installer (e.g., `NVIDIA ChatRTX.exe`) which installs the software into a default application data directory, not a user-specified `C:\ChatRTX` directory via a batch file.
The command `chatrtx pull --model default` for downloading the AI model is invented. ChatRTX does not use a `pull` command for model management in this manner.

The command `chatrtx run --port 8080` for starting the chatbot server is invented. ChatRTX does not use a `run` command like this, and its default server port is typically 8000, not 8080, unless configured through its UI. The related example command prompt outputs are also fabricated.

title: How to Use Physical Security Keys with Your Work Computer
problems: The URL `https://accounts.google.com/credentialprovider` is incorrect for setting up the Google Credential Provider for Windows or registering a security key for Windows login via GCPW. The Google Credential Provider for Windows is a software that must be downloaded and installed on a Windows computer, not configured via this web page to register security keys directly for Windows.

The entire flow described in Steps 3 through 6, including specific UI elements like 'Set up security key for Windows' page, 'Add a security key' heading, 'Sign in' button on that page, 'Register a new key', 'Key registered' confirmation, and the option 'Use this key as default for sign-in', describes the process of registering a security key for a *Google account* through its general security settings (e.g., `myaccount.google.com/security/signinoptions/security-key`). This is not the setup or configuration process for the 'Credential Provider for Windows' tool itself, nor does it directly enable the key for Windows login *via GCPW* without the critical step of installing the GCPW software on the computer. The article completely omits the necessary installation of the 'Credential Provider for Windows' software.

title: Create a clear README in 10 minutes with GitHub Copilot
problems: The claim that GitHub Copilot is "free for individuals" is broadly incorrect. While it is free for verified students, teachers, and maintainers of popular open-source projects, it is a paid subscription for most individual users. This is a fabricated plan claim stated as fact.

The article states that users can "use the shortcut Ctrl+I (Windows/Linux) or Cmd+I (Mac)" to open the GitHub Copilot chat panel in the GitHub.com web editor. This shortcut does not open the Copilot chat panel in the GitHub.com web editor; the chat is activated by clicking the dedicated Copilot icon. This is a fabricated UI interaction/shortcut.

title: How to use Qwen Chat to plan a weekend road trip in Australia without getting lost
problems: In Step 4, the instruction to "look for a “Show full route” link or button inside the reply" is fabricated. Qwen Chat's interface does not embed interactive buttons or links within its text responses that expand content.

In Step 5, the instruction to "look for a “More suggestions” button" is fabricated. Qwen Chat does not typically offer interactive buttons within its text output to generate more suggestions; users typically achieve this by prompting again.

In Step 6, the instruction to "look for a “Download PDF” button at the bottom of the reply" is fabricated. Qwen Chat, like most general chat LLMs, does not provide a direct PDF download button for its responses; users would copy text and convert it externally.

In Step 7, the claim "You'll know it worked when you see a green checkmark list with no red flags" is fabricated. Qwen Chat outputs plain text, not visually rendered "green checkmark lists" or other specific color/icon styling for its responses.

title: Let Copilot turn your messy notes into a clean project plan
problems: Invented URL / domain: The article instructs users to go to "copilot.github.com" to open Copilot Chat. This URL is incorrect for accessing a direct web-based chat interface for GitHub Copilot. GitHub Copilot Chat is primarily an integration within IDEs (like VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains IDEs) or accessed within github.com itself, not via a standalone web portal at 'copilot.github.com'.

UI elements/buttons/menus/pages described for a named product that do not exist: Following the incorrect URL, the article describes finding a button like "Open Copilot Chat" or "Start chatting" in the top-right corner, leading to a chat panel sliding in from the right. This specific user interface and access method for a direct chat portal do not exist for GitHub Copilot at the described 'copilot.github.com' location.

title: Organise your favourite recipes with Perplexity Q&A
problems: The article describes a specific UI element and functionality for Perplexity Spaces that does not exist: a command to explicitly "Save this as a recipe in My Recipe Book" that results in a confirmation message like "Added to your space: Pumpkin Soup" or a "Saved" badge/list of recipes in the space sidebar. Perplexity Spaces maintain chat history context but do not offer a structured saving mechanism for individual 'items' like recipes with dedicated confirmations or UI listings.

The claim that one can "tag it with keywords like “vegan”, “quick”, or “weeknight”" in a structured way within Perplexity Spaces is incorrect. While users can include keywords in their prompts, Perplexity does not have a native feature to 'tag' individual entries for structured retrieval or organization within a space beyond its conversational context understanding.

title: Perform a basic SWOT analysis with Grok to evaluate a project
problems: The claim of a 'free xAI Grok account' is incorrect. Grok is currently available exclusively to X Premium+ subscribers, which is a paid subscription. It is not offered as a standalone free service.

The URL 'https://grok.com' is incorrectly presented as the primary sign-up or access point for a Grok account. While 'grok.com' redirects to X.com/grok, users access Grok through the X platform (x.com or the X app) as part of their Premium+ subscription, not by creating an account directly at 'grok.com'. There is no standalone 'Grok app' separate from the X app for access as implied.

title: Getting started with Perplexity for answers that show their sources
problems: The 'Focus' mode menu description lists 'No web (local only)' as an option. Perplexity's 'Focus' modes are for filtering web sources (e.g., 'Academic', 'YouTube', 'Reddit'). There is no standard 'No web (local only)' option in the 'Focus' dropdown for general queries. While Perplexity has features related to local documents, they are not presented as a 'Focus' filter for web search in this manner.

title: Organise Your Photos with Apple Intelligence: Smart Search & Editing
problems: The article describes an "Object Eraser" tool in Apple Photos that allows users to brush over any small, unwanted objects like "a stray person" or "rubbish bin" for seamless removal. While iOS 18 introduces a "Clean Up" tool, it is designed for removing distracting *background elements* and is not a general, brush-based object removal tool like the one described, which more closely resembles features found in Google Photos' Magic Eraser or Samsung's Object Eraser. This feature, with the described UI and functionality, does not exist in Apple Photos.

title: Get realistic renovation prices fast with Perplexity AI
problems: The article describes a UI element in Step 2: "After the search loads, look for a box with a plus sign (+) or a prompt that says “Ask anything…”. Tap or click it to start a new question." Perplexity does not have a 'box with a plus sign (+)' for starting a new question within an existing search thread. The input field at the bottom is for follow-up questions and is labeled 'Ask a follow-up' or similar.

The article describes a UI element in Step 3: "Look for a button or link that says “Follow-up” or “Ask a follow-up” near the top right of the answer. Tap or click it to continue the conversation." Perplexity does not have a 'Follow-up' or 'Ask a follow-up' button or link located at the top right of an answer. Follow-up questions are entered into an input box at the bottom of the conversation.

title: Plan Your Next Weekend Getaway or Event with Claude's Help
problems: The claim that there is a 'download button' (down-arrow icon) to save Claude's response as a .txt file is fabricated. Claude's web interface (claude.ai) does not currently offer a direct download feature for chat responses; users must copy the text manually.

title: Quickly Research Any Topic and Summarise Web Pages with Microsoft Copilot in Edge
problems: The article describes a UI element 'dropdown menu at the top' of the Copilot sidebar with options like 'Chat', 'Compose', and 'Summarise' in Step 2. Copilot in Microsoft Edge does not have such a dropdown menu to select summarization as a distinct mode. Summarization is typically offered via a contextual button or prompt within the chat interface itself, not a mode selector.

The article claims in Step 6 that users can 'Ask Copilot to save it by typing: “Save this summary to my notes.”' and that a confirmation like 'Summary saved.' will appear. Copilot in Edge does not have a specific 'save to notes' command that triggers a 'Summary saved' confirmation, nor does it have a dedicated 'notes' feature for summaries. While chat history is retained (for signed-in users), this specific interaction is fabricated.

title: Turn messy phone photos into a family album with Google Photos AI
problems: The article describes the Google Photos bottom navigation bar as having five icons: "Photos, Search, Albums, Utilities, and Library". The current Google Photos app typically has four main bottom navigation icons (Photos, Search, Sharing, Library), with "Albums" and "Utilities" being sub-sections usually found within the "Library" tab.

The 'Common mistakes' section suggests that if 'People & pets' doesn't appear, users should 'tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner and choose Refresh'. There is no 'Refresh' option in the Google Photos app's three-dot menu (or anywhere else in that context) that would make the 'People & pets' section appear.

The 'Common mistakes' section advises users to 'try scanning smaller folders first (for example, just the last six months of photos)' if the app runs slowly. Google Photos does not provide users with the ability to selectively scan specific folders or date ranges for its face grouping feature; it processes the entire synced library.

title: Set up Alexa+ to monitor and report daily energy usage
problems: The 'Alexa+ Energy Usage' skill described in Step 3 does not exist as a general skill required to enable energy monitoring for compatible devices, including Amazon's own Smart Plugs. Amazon Smart Plugs offer native energy reporting, and third-party devices require their specific manufacturer's skill, not a generic 'Alexa+ Energy Usage' skill.

title: Set Up Qwen Chat for Automated E-commerce FAQs
problems: The article describes a specific Alibaba Cloud service named "Qwen Chat" that does not exist. While Alibaba Cloud offers Qwen large language models and services to build chatbots (like Machine Learning Platform for AI or Intelligent Customer Service), there is no standalone product called "Qwen Chat" that directly provides a dedicated console for creating projects, managing a "Prompt Library" with UI elements like "Add New Prompt" buttons, generating API keys specifically for a "Qwen Chat project," and directly retrieving a "website embed code" for a chat widget, as depicted in the step-by-step guide. The UI elements and specific workflow attributed to "Qwen Chat" are fabricated for a product that is not offered by Alibaba Cloud under this name with these direct features.

The described UI elements such as a dedicated "Qwen Chat service page" within the Alibaba Cloud console, "Create New Project" buttons on this page, a "Prompt Library" section within the project dashboard, and a "Deployment" or "Website Embed" section to retrieve an embeddable chat widget code are specific to a non-existent product named "Qwen Chat."

title: Turn your messy meeting notes into a polished report with Le Chat in 5 minutes
problems: The claim "Optional: a paid Le Chat plan if you want longer reports or more features later" is fabricated. While Mistral offers paid API access for developers using their models, there is no direct 'paid Le Chat plan' available for the consumer-facing Le Chat web interface that would unlock features like 'longer reports' within that UI.

title: Turn holiday voice memos into a polished travel blog post using NVIDIA ChatRTX
problems: The article claims NVIDIA ChatRTX has a 'paperclip or upload icon' for audio files and can directly transcribe them, showing messages like 'Uploading file…' and 'Transcribing audio…'. NVIDIA ChatRTX is a text-based RAG LLM demo and does not possess built-in audio transcription features or a dedicated UI for uploading and transcribing audio files.

The article states there is a 'download or export button' in the ChatRTX interface with options like 'Export as text file' for the polished blog post. While users can copy text from the chat, the NVIDIA ChatRTX tech demo does not include a specific UI button for exporting chat output as a text file.

title: Sharpen Old Videos with NVIDIA AI Super-Resolution Online
problems: The article describes a specific 'NVIDIA AI Super-Resolution online demo' with detailed UI elements (e.g., 'Upload your video' button, 'Upscaling Factor' dropdown with '2x' or '4x' options, 'Process' button, side-by-side comparison, 'Download' button) and claims it is a free, public, online tool directly offered and hosted by NVIDIA ('official NVIDIA website,' 'NVIDIA showcases its innovative AI tools for anyone to try,' 'send your video and settings to NVIDIA's AI servers'). NVIDIA does not provide a publicly accessible, free, general video super-resolution online demo with this described user interface and workflow directly on its official website for arbitrary user video uploads. While NVIDIA technology powers many super-resolution solutions, the existence of such an official, NVIDIA-hosted, consumer-facing online demo is fabricated.

title: Check your resume for ATS-friendly keywords using Hugging Face’s Inference API
problems: The article describes navigating to 'Products' in the top menu on Hugging Face and clicking 'Inference API'. The correct menu item is 'Solutions', not 'Products'.

The article claims that after opening the 'Inference API' page, users will 'see a page with a text box and a list of AI models' where they can 'paste your job ad and resume'. The general Hugging Face Inference API page is informational and does not immediately present a text box for interaction or a list of models to paste content into.

The article instructs users to 'In the text box, type or paste this model name exactly: microsoft/Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct. Then press Enter or click Submit.' on the Inference API page. There is no such text box on the general Inference API page to load a model by typing its name. Users must navigate to the specific model's page (e.g., by searching) and use its dedicated 'Hosted Inference API' widget.

The article states, 'You'll know it worked when you see a text box that says Enter your prompt here and a button that says Submit' as the confirmation for opening the general 'Inference API' page. This specific interactive interface (text box for prompt and submit button) is found on an individual model's hosted inference page, not the general Inference API overview page.

title: Clear Up Blurry iPhone Photos with Apple Intelligence
problems: The article falsely attributes the existing 'Enhance' (magic wand) button and the 'Sharpen' slider in the Photos app as explicit features powered by Apple Intelligence for fixing blurry photos. While Apple Intelligence introduces a 'Clean Up' tool for object removal in Photos, Apple has not announced that the traditional 'Enhance' and 'Sharpen' tools are part of the Apple Intelligence suite, nor are they new capabilities enabled by it. These tools have existed in the Photos app for many iOS versions prior to Apple Intelligence.

title: Clean up a messy customer list in Excel with Copilot in under 2 minutes
problems: The article describes a UI/feature where Copilot in Excel can directly "remove the duplicate rows" after a user's conversational command and an "approve" button within the Copilot pane. As of current knowledge, Copilot for Microsoft 365 in Excel can identify duplicates, provide insights, and suggest formulas, but it does not have the capability to directly execute data manipulation actions like deleting rows from the spreadsheet based on a chat command and a subsequent approval within its interface. Users would still need to apply Excel's native features (e.g., 'Remove Duplicates' feature or a formula Copilot might suggest) to perform the actual deletion.

title: Use NVIDIA ChatRTX to create a personal study buddy that quizzes any PDF
problems: The NVIDIA ChatRTX web interface on the NVIDIA AI Playground (https://www.nvidia.com/ai-playground) does not feature a 'paper-clip icon', 'Upload' button, or 'Attach file' option to directly upload arbitrary PDF documents. This functionality, as described, is not available in the web-based ChatRTX playground.

The described UI elements and flow for file upload, including a 'file-chooser window', 'PDF upload bar', and a 'tiny chip' displaying the filename under the chat input, are fabricated for the NVIDIA ChatRTX web interface.
The claim of ChatRTX acknowledging an uploaded PDF with text like 'I’ve loaded the PDF' within the web interface is fabricated, as the described upload mechanism does not exist.

References to a 'free-plan limit (usually a few hundred megabytes)' for file uploads are fabricated, as there is no general file upload feature for arbitrary PDFs on the NVIDIA AI Playground's ChatRTX, nor a specific pricing tier for it in this context.

The existence of a 'Download button' (downward-arrow icon) near the top-right of the chat pane offering options like 'Save as PDF' for the entire chat output on the NVIDIA AI Playground is fabricated. While 'Copy to clipboard' is common, a specific 'Save as PDF' for chat logs is not a standard feature there.

title: Use Qwen Chat to draft a thank-you note after a job interview
problems: The URL 'qwen.chat' for signing up to Qwen Chat is incorrect. The official entry point for Qwen (Tongyi Qianwen) is typically through Alibaba Cloud or a specific 'tongyi.aliyun.com' domain, not 'qwen.chat'.

title: Turn one sentence into a ready-to-use study timetable with Qwen Chat
problems: The article claims that Qwen Chat's generated 'colour-coded labels' (e.g., '🔴 Maths') will result in study blocks appearing 'with the right colour' when copied and pasted into a calendar application. This is fabricated functionality; standard calendar applications do not interpret emoji or textual colour indicators from a chat interface as instructions for event colors, which must be set manually by the user within the calendar app.

title: How to Add an Alibaba Cloud AI Chatbot to Your WordPress Site
problems: The URL `https://chatbot.alibabacloud.com/widget.js` for embedding a generic Alibaba Cloud AI Chatbot widget is invented. Alibaba Cloud's Intelligent Service Robot (ISR) service primarily offers API integrations and SDKs for building custom UIs, rather than a single, publicly hosted `<script src="..."></script>` widget from a generic subdomain that provides a full, pre-built chat bubble and UI.

title: How to Use Amazon's Conversational Alexa+ at Home
problems: The article states that Alexa+ conversational features 'can be turned on in the Alexa app settings under 'Conversational Mode' or 'Generative AI Features''. While Alexa+ (Amazon's generative AI for Alexa) is real and offers advanced conversational capabilities, there is no widely available, named 'Conversational Mode' or 'Generative AI Features' toggle in the Alexa app settings for users to explicitly enable or disable this core functionality. These features are typically rolled out by default to eligible devices/accounts, or accessible through specific verbal commands or preview programs, rather than a distinct UI setting as described.

title: How to set ChatGPT custom instructions so it answers your way
problems: The article suggests looking for 'a tab labelled "About Me" or similar' if the Custom Instructions interface looks different. ChatGPT's Custom Instructions feature does not use tabs within its interface; it consistently presents two distinct text boxes without tabs.

title: How to use Claude Artifacts to create and preview your work
problems: The article describes a specific 'Artifacts button' in the chat toolbar that users must click to 'turn on' or 'reveal' the Artifacts pane (Step 2 and Common mistakes). In reality, Claude's Artifacts pane typically appears dynamically on the right side of the screen when an artifact is generated, or it is a persistently available and collapsible UI element, rather than requiring an explicit 'turn on' button click in the main chat toolbar as a prerequisite to generating an artifact.

title: How to Use ChatGPT's Memory to Remember Your Unique Preferences
problems: The statement 'This feature may be part of a paid plan for some users' when discussing viewing and organizing ChatGPT memories is misleading. OpenAI's official policy is that the Memory feature, including the ability to view and organize memories, is rolling out to BOTH ChatGPT Free and Plus users on an opt-in basis. Therefore, it is not a feature restricted to or potentially restricted to paid plans for certain users, but rather universally available to all users who opt-in.

title: Digitise Handwritten Notes into Editable Text with AI
problems: The article claims that in Microsoft Lens, after taking a photo, 'you might see a 'Text' option at the bottom of the screen to view the extracted text'. In Microsoft Lens, the 'Text' option on the editing screen is used for *adding* text to the image, not for viewing the OCR-extracted text. To view or use the extracted text, users typically need to export to a format like Microsoft Word or use the Immersive Reader feature, rather than seeing a direct 'Text' option at the bottom for viewing.

title: Draft quick text messages with Apple Intelligence’s predictive writing
problems: The claim that "On some iPhones, the predictions might appear below the message field instead of above the keyboard" is incorrect. In the Messages app on iOS, the predictive text bar (QuickType) always appears above the keyboard, directly below the message input field. It does not appear below the message field.

title: Unlock Real-Time Insights with Grok on X
problems: UI elements/buttons/menus/pages described for a named product that do not exist: The article describes a 'Grok icon... often located near the bottom navigation bar on mobile or in the left sidebar on the website'. Grok is typically accessed within the X app or website via the search/explore tab or through dedicated cards in the 'For You' feed, not by a persistent, standalone 'Grok icon' in the primary bottom navigation bar or left sidebar as implied by the description.

title: How to Lock In Lower AI Costs with Reserved Capacity
problems: The article claims that for ChatGPT, users should look for 'names with mini in them' as the light model option at the top of the chat window. While ChatGPT offers a lighter model (GPT-3.5) and developer-focused 'mini' models exist, the general user interface for ChatGPT Plus or free users does not present a model option explicitly labeled 'mini' in the same way Gemini uses 'Flash' or Claude uses 'Haiku' at the top of the chat window.

title: Write a polite complaint email with Le Chat in minutes
problems: The article mentions 'Open the Le Chat app on your phone' and 'Access to Le Chat (web or mobile app)'. Le Chat is a web-based interface provided by Mistral AI, accessible via a web browser on both desktop and mobile devices. There is no official, dedicated 'Le Chat app' for mobile phones released by Mistral AI, implying a non-existent UI/access method.

title: Chat and Create with Meta AI on Instagram and Messenger
problems: The claim 'On the free plan, you may also have daily limits on how many images you can generate' implies a tiered 'free plan' and potentially paid plans for Meta AI image generation. Meta AI's image generation is a free feature within Instagram and Messenger, and there are no publicly advertised 'plans' or stated daily limits that differentiate it from other non-existent paid tiers.

title: Turn a messy customer review into a polished testimonial with Cohere
problems: The article describes looking for a 'chat bubble or a box that says “Start a new chat” in the middle of the screen' on the Cohere dashboard after signing in. While Cohere does offer a chat model, its current UI typically requires users to navigate to the 'Playground' from the sidebar and then select the 'Chat' model. There isn't a general 'Start a new chat' button or chat bubble prominently in the middle of the main dashboard screen as described, making this UI element description inaccurate or fabricated.

title: Use Meta AI to organise your next garage sale in 5 simple steps
problems: The UI description for starting a new chat in Step 1, 'Tap the Chat icon on the Meta homepage, then press the + New conversation button,' does not accurately reflect the interface of Meta AI (meta.ai) or its integrations within Meta's platforms. On meta.ai, users land directly on the chat interface, and on other platforms, the access point is typically different from a generic 'Chat icon on the Meta homepage' leading to a '+ New conversation' button for the AI.

title: Start Using Microsoft Copilot in Word, Excel, and Outlook
problems: The description in 'Step 1 — Start a draft in Word' of a 'small, colourful icon on the page' as a clickable 'Copilot button' that opens a 'chat box directly within your document' to start a draft is not representative of the typical user interface for Microsoft Copilot in a new Word document. The common experience is to interact with a text prompt within the document itself (e.g., 'Draft with Copilot') or to activate a side panel from the Word ribbon.

title: Turn a quick voice memo into a structured meeting summary with Copilot
problems: The URL copilot.github.com is invented — the real GitHub Copilot chat URL is github.com/copilot or copilot.microsoft.com, not copilot.github.com

GitHub Copilot is a code-focused AI assistant and does not function as a general-purpose chat that meets summaries from voice memos as described — the described workflow (paste a voice memo, get a structured meeting summary with action items) attributes a general meeting-summarization use case to GitHub Copilot that is not its intended/promoted function
